analysis.title: ETF Market Pulse Week 44 - Value in the Driver's Seat: Bulgaria Surges, Brazil Stumbles
key_insights: Last week's ETF returns showed a rotation away from US Growth and speculative assets toward cheaper equity segments. US Growth fell 1.7% on renewed concerns over stretched tech valuations and the sustainability of AI-related capex.
EM equities fell 2.0%, which the report attributes to higher US yields.
Bitcoin fell 5.7%, the main laggard. The risk-off move triggered a sharp unwind of leveraged crypto derivatives, and the Binance security incident added selling pressure and accelerated liquidations.
US Value and US Small Caps each gained 1.3%. European equities gained 1.5%, helped by value-heavy, lower-tech exposure that gave relative insulation from the US tech sell-off.

The Expat Bulgaria SOFIX UCITS ETF rose 13% in USD, the top performer. Drivers were its removal from the FATF grey list (Oct 30) and positioning ahead of MSCI's planned upgrade to Frontier Market status. Limited market liquidity amplified the inflow-driven gains.
Brazil-focused equity ETFs were among the main laggards after a sharp political and fiscal repricing. Lula's narrow runoff victory challenged expectations of a more market-friendly policy shift.

In fixed income, investors redeemed Bloomberg US Treasury Bills 1-3 Months exposure and added to iBoxx USD Investment Grade Corporate Bonds. Despite the Fed's hawkish pause, flows suggest investors saw front-end cash yields as close to their peak and moved out the curve to lock in IG corporate yields.

In equities, MSCI Brazil 25/50 saw heavy redemptions (-$1,063.5m, -9.8% of AuM) on post-election fiscal concerns. Creations favored S&P 500 Financials and Health Care, and MSCI World ESG Broad CTB Select also saw strong creations.
Largest absolute weekly inflows were S&P 500 (+$8,081.2m) and Nasdaq 100 (+$7,165.8m). Russell 1000 Value had the largest outflow of the listed names (-$1,572.6m).

New launches in Europe: Amundi repriced its swap-based MSCI ACWI ETF at 9bp vs 45bp for its existing ETF. VanEck launched a UCITS China Semiconductor ETF on a 10%-capped, ESG-screened index. iShares launched the fourth active global defence UCITS ETF, and State Street added a 13th global high-yield UCITS ETF.
New launches in the US: AB added another US active equity ETF (AB US Research Advanced ETF), and Hartford launched the first active developed-markets ex-North America growth ETF.

sector_views.rationale: The report's cross-sectional Z-score framework, based on 1-week USD returns and 20-day realised volatility, shows attractive rewards for US Value, Eurozone equities and US Small Caps.
US Growth fell 1.7% on concerns over stretched tech valuations and the sustainability of AI-related capex.
Creations favored S&P 500 Financials and Health Care, combining higher-for-longer/value exposure with defensive earnings.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held policy with a hawkish tone. ETF flows suggest investors viewed front-end cash yields as near a peak and moved into IG corporate bonds.

crypto_views: Bitcoin (IBIT) fell 5.7% last week as a risk-off move unwound leveraged crypto derivatives.
The Binance security incident added to selling pressure and accelerated liquidations.
The report's chart titles describe an extended Bitcoin drawdown and crypto return asymmetry.
risk_factors: Stretched tech valuations and the sustainability of AI-related capex.
Higher US yields weighing on EM equities.
Brazil's political and fiscal outlook after the narrow runoff result.
Leveraged crypto derivative unwinds and the Binance security incident.
Thin liquidity in Bulgaria can amplify moves in both directions.
vol_and_positioning: Leveraged crypto derivatives saw a sharp unwind during the risk-off move, with accelerated liquidations.
Rotation out of US Growth and speculative assets into cheaper equity segments, with creations in S&P 500 Financials and Health Care.
Bulgaria's limited liquidity amplified inflow-driven gains ahead of MSCI's planned Frontier Market upgrade.
Investors rotated out of T-Bills (Bloomberg US Treasury Bills 1-3 Months, ICE 0-3 Month, ICE Short US Treasury) and into IG corporate credit (iBoxx USD Liquid IG, +$1,678.3m, 4.0% of AuM).
geopolitical: Lula's narrow runoff victory in Brazil's election challenged expectations of a more market-friendly policy shift and triggered a political and fiscal repricing.
Bulgaria was removed from the FATF grey list on Oct 30.
